page: Microsoft Azure D8ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. Storage is supported by 307 GB of local disk capacity, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Most other computational workloads, including Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, and cryptography tests, perform in the average range. However, memory subsystem performance presents notable tradeoffs. While cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 514.81 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths fall into the bottom 25% at 39.11 GB/sec and 22.63 GB/sec respectively. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also registers as weak.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D8ads_v5 balances dedicated compute resources with a standard memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a resource-dense option for general-purpose workloads that do not require continuous high-throughput memory access. It is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, Redis key-value stores, database operations, and light LLM inference tasks using small models.
